headline: The bounce came entirely out of the wreckage — semis +3.6%, AMD +11% — paid for by liquidating the defensive winners, while a 95th-percentile dollar and a +5bp front end say nothing has actually been fixed.
summary: Yesterday's read was a global funding event; today was a violent mean-reversion squeeze inside it. QQQ +1.4%, SMH +3.6%, SOXX +3.5%, AMD +11.0%, TSM +6.3%, MU +5.1%, ASML +5.0%, NVDA +2.8%, and the AI-power complex ripped — VST +10.6%, ETN +4.5%, CEG +4.3%, URA +4.4%. But the S&P only managed +0.3% because the money came out of the exact names that have been holding the tape up: XLP -1.3%, UPS -2.5%, IHI -2.4%, DHI -3.4%, HD -1.8%, WMT -1.7%, XRT -1.7%, KIE -1.7%, ITB -2.1%. RSP/SPY fell 0.7% for the first time in this drawdown even as its z-score stays a preposterous 4.16. High-beta/low-vol +3.6%, growth/value +1.6%, SMH/SPY +3.3%. That is a positioning unwind, not a re-risking: the risk regime actually deteriorated to -23 from -20.

The reason it deteriorated is the two things that did not cooperate. First, the dollar. DXY +0.7% to 102.28, now the 95th percentile of its year, with EURUSD -0.8% to 1.1143 (1.5th percentile), GBPUSD -0.9%, AUDUSD -1.9%, USDCAD +1.1%, USDKRW +1.8%, USDBRL +0.7% to 5.4959 — +10.3% on the month at z=2.99 with acceleration 2.56. Second, rates. Strong payroll-adjacent data pushed the 2y +5bp to 4.51 and the 5y +5bp to 4.64, the 10y real yield +3bp to 2.63, and 2s10s down to 35bp, the 28th percentile. TLT was flat (-0.0%) on an up day for equities for the second straight session. The 30y sits at 5.26% and the 30y mortgage at 7.18%, the 85th percentile. Duration is still refusing to hedge equity risk, which means the entire cushion has to come from the oil windfall — Brent 97.76 still -16.9% on the week, RBOB -14.4% on the month — and from earnings, not from discount rates.

The vol surface says do not trust the rally. VIX fell 9.0% to 25.64 but is still +70.0% on the month with z=2.8 and 40% above its 200-day. VIX/VIX3M at 1.0423 is still inverted and sits in the 82nd percentile. And SKEW rose another 2.8% to 153.55, +8.3% on the month: somebody is paying up for tail protection into a falling spot VIX. Credit agrees. HYG was -0.1% on a green equity day, sits at the 31st percentile, and HYG/IEF is -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06 and rolling over. Credit & vol remains the worst composite on the board at -66. Meanwhile the capex/industrial chain never participated in the bounce in any durable way: CAT -31.2% on the month at z=-3.52 and the 3rd percentile, GRID -14.2%, GEV -22.3%, AVGO at the 1st percentile of its 52-week range, ORCL at the 1st.

Where it is genuinely working is the dispersion trade, and it widened again. India: Sensex +2.6%, INDA +1.7% and +10.4% on the month at z=2.35 with acceleration 2.91, financed by USDINR -2.6% at z=-2.55. Mexico: IPC at the 98th percentile, +10.4% on the month. Against that, Brazil is a slow-motion accident — EWZ -24.5% on the month at z=-3.25, Bovespa z=-3.45, the currency at a 3-sigma move. Gold miners are the other live beta: GDX +2.2% today and +13.6% on the week with gold -1.5% on the month, pushing GDX/gold +3.0% to the 78th percentile. EEM/SPY at z=-1.64 is hiding a 35-point internal gap. Trade the spread, not the index.

good.text: Volatility came in hard: VIX -9.0% to 25.64, VIX3M -3.7% to 24.60, MOVE -5.3% to 92.77. The bond-vol relief matters more than the equity-vol relief — MOVE has now unwound 9.5% on the month.

The epicentre bounced on real volume, not just a drift: SMH +3.6%, SOXX +3.5%, AMD +11.0%, TSM +6.3%, MU +5.1%, ASML +5.0%, NVDA +2.8%. Bargain-hunting in memory and foundry after a 25-30% monthly drawdown.

Asia stopped exporting the damage. EWY +4.1%, EWT +3.9%, HSI +3.7%, EEM +2.2%, FXI flat after +5.7% on the week — the EM equity complex absorbed Korea's -5.3% cash session and still closed green in ADR form.

India keeps compounding: Sensex +2.6%, INDA +1.7% and +10.4% on the month at z=2.35 with acceleration 2.91, with USDINR -0.7% today and -2.6% on the month at z=-2.55. A rare EM where the currency and the equity are pulling the same direction.
Gold miners are outrunning the metal: GDX +2.2% and +13.6% on the week, GDXJ +2.8%, NEM +13.4% on the week, GDX/GOLD +3.0% to the 78th percentile while gold itself is -1.5% on the month.

The energy windfall is intact even with crude stabilising: WTI -0.2% at 90.34 and Brent -0.5% at 97.76 after a 13-17% weekly collapse, gasoline -14.4% on the month at z=-1.39. That is a direct, ongoing transfer to the consumer and the CPI print.

bad.text: The dollar is the tightening now. DXY +0.7% to 102.28 at the 95th percentile, EURUSD -0.8% to 1.1143 at the 1.5th percentile of its year, GBPUSD -0.9%, AUDUSD -1.9%, USDCAD +1.1%, USDKRW +1.8%. A risk-asset bounce on a stronger dollar is a squeeze, not a turn.

Brazil is accelerating the wrong way: USDBRL +0.7% to 5.4959, +10.3% on the month at z=2.99 with acceleration z=2.56 and turning up; EWZ -24.5% on the month at z=-3.25; Bovespa z=-3.45 with acceleration -3.63. This is now the single most stressed cross in the dataset.

Yields backed up on the strong data and duration still will not hedge: 2y +5bp to 4.51, 5y +5bp to 4.64, 10y real yield +3bp to 2.63, 2s10s -3bp to 35bp (28th percentile), TLT flat on an up equity day, 30y mortgage 7.18% at the 85th percentile.
Tail demand rose while spot vol fell — SKEW +2.8% to 153.55 and +8.3% on the month, VIX/VIX3M still inverted at 1.0423 in the 82nd percentile. Someone is buying crash protection into the rally.
Credit refused to join: HYG -0.1% on a green day and at the 31st percentile, HYG/IEF -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06 and rolling over, LQD -0.1%. Credit & vol is the worst composite at -66.

The defensive cushion cracked for the first time: XLP -1.3%, UPS -2.5%, IHI -2.4%, HD -1.8%, WMT -1.7%, XRT -1.7%, DHI -3.4%, and RSP/SPY -0.7%. If the breadth trade unwinds alongside a still-broken momentum complex (MTUM z=-3.79, CAT z=-3.52), there is no leadership left.

trades.name: Long India / short Brazil
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWZ — EM dispersion, 35pts and widening
trades.expr: Buy INDA, short EWZ, dollar-neutral notional. Overlay: short USDBRL vol or own 3m USDBRL calls as the hedge leg if you cannot short EWZ.
trades.thesis: EM is not one asset. India has a falling dollar cross (USDINR -2.6% on the month, z=-2.55) funding a 10.4% monthly equity gain; Brazil has a 3-sigma currency blowout funding a 24.5% monthly equity collapse. These are the two tails of the same EEM index that screens as merely 'weak' at z=-1.64.
trades.trigger: INDA +1.7% today, z=2.35, acceleration 2.91, turning_up; EWZ -24.5% on the month at z=-3.25 with acceleration -3.14 and USDBRL still turning up at z=2.99.
trades.stop: USDBRL reverses back below 5.25 (fiscal/political relief) or INDA's relative-strength-vs-S&P flips from +16.7% 1m to negative. Exit on a 6% adverse move in the spread.
trades.target: Another 10-12% of spread, i.e. INDA toward its 52-week highs while EWZ holds the 11th percentile.

trades.name: Short AUD/USD
trades.line: Short AUDUSD — dollar squeeze plus copper rolling over
trades.expr: Short spot AUDUSD at 0.6868, or buy 2-month 0.6700 AUD puts. Equity-sleeve alternative: short FXA.
trades.thesis: The second leg of this correction is a funding event, not an equity event. DXY at the 95th percentile with EURUSD at the 1.5th and AUD as the highest-beta G10 proxy to both Chinese metals demand and global risk appetite. Copper -5.1% on the month and COPX -14.8% remove the terms-of-trade support.
trades.trigger: AUDUSD -1.9% today and -2.3% on the week, rolling over, 2.6% below its 200-day; AUDJPY -1.9% to 108.79; DXY +0.7% and 2.6% above its 200-day.
trades.stop: Close above 0.7020, or DXY breaking back under 101.0 with copper reclaiming 6.50.

trades.name: Buy the tail into the squeeze
trades.line: Own Dec/Jan SPX put spreads while VIX bleeds -9%
trades.expr: Buy Dec/Jan SPY 700/640 put spreads (SPX 7000/6400 equivalent) funded by selling 1-month 775 calls. Alternative: Dec VIX 30/45 call spread.
trades.thesis: Spot vol is deflating while the surface is screaming. A 9% VIX drop on a 0.3% S&P day with the term structure still inverted and SKEW making new highs is the signature of dealers selling front vol into persistent institutional tail demand. You are being paid to own the gap.
trades.trigger: VIX -9.0% to 25.64 but still +70.0% on the month at z=2.8; VIX/VIX3M 1.0423, 82nd percentile, still backwardated; SKEW +2.8% to 153.55; HYG/IEF at z=-2.06 and rolling over has not confirmed any of the equity bounce.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M closes below 0.92 (contango restored) and HYG/IEF turns up — then the hedge is a pure cost and you cut it.
trades.target: SPY 660-680 retest (the -10% level from the September highs), VIX 35+.

trades.name: Short high yield vs Treasuries
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF — spot HY still pretending
trades.expr: Short HYG, long IEF on matched notional; or buy Jan HYG 75 puts. Cleaner institutional version: buy CDX HY protection.
trades.thesis: HYG price at 77.23 is at the 31st percentile of its year and has gone nowhere while equity vol has risen 70% in a month. The ratio to Treasuries has already broken — -2.9% on the month at z=-2.06, rolling over. Either equity vol mean-reverts hard or HY catches down. Given the dollar and the front-end back-up, the latter is more likely.
trades.trigger: HYG -0.1% on a day QQQ rose 1.4%; BKLN only +0.2%; credit & vol composite at -66, the worst on the board, versus a risk regime of -23.
trades.stop: HYG closes above 78.50 with HYG/IEF z-score back above -0.5, or VIX sustains below 20.
trades.target: HYG 74.50, roughly 300bp of ratio underperformance versus IEF.

trades.name: Short the crowded defensive
trades.line: Short MCD — z=3.84, acceleration 3.98, already rolling over
trades.expr: Short MCD outright at 276.52, or buy Jan 270/245 put spreads. Pair version: short MCD vs long XLV if you want sector-neutral.
trades.thesis: MCD is the most statistically extended name in the dataset: +19.8% on the month at z=3.84 with acceleration z=3.98, and the trend state has already flipped to rolling_over. It is a crowded flight-to-safety trade in a stock with negative 1-year performance (-5.0%) and relative strength vs the S&P already marked 'down'. The defensive bid cracked today.
trades.trigger: The whole staples/bond-proxy cohort got liquidated on the semi squeeze — XLP -1.3%, WMT -1.7%, HD -1.8%, UPS -2.5%, RSP/SPY -0.7% for the first time in this drawdown.
trades.stop: MCD closes above 285 or VIX reclaims 30 (genuine flight-to-safety resumption validates the crowding).
trades.target: 255, back to the 200-day it is only 1.2% below.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH on the 3.6% ratio give-back
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, equal dollar notional. Size for 2x realised vol of the ratio — this pair moves.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is being re-rated from hardware to software. IGV/SMH is +21.3% on the month and +20.9% on three months, turning up, yet it still sits at only the 44th percentile of its 52-week range after a -31.7% year — plenty of room. Semis remain structurally broken: SOXX -29.7% on the month at z=-3.2, SMH/SPY at z=-3.48, AVGO at the 1st percentile, MU -36.6% on the month.
trades.trigger: The ratio gave back 3.6% today on the memory/foundry squeeze (AMD +11%, TSM +6.3%, MU +5.1%). That is your entry, not your refutation — IGV was only -0.1% and still sits 5.1% above its 200-day while SMH is 10.9% below its own.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH breaks back below 0.195, or SMH reclaims its 200-day (roughly 520).

trades.name: Gold miners over bullion
trades.line: Long GDX vs short GLD — operating leverage, gold flat
trades.expr: Long GDX (or GDXJ for more beta), short GLD at a 1:1 dollar notional. Keep it small; both legs are volatile.
trades.thesis: Gold is -1.5% on the month and -9.5% below its 200-day, yet miners are +2.5% on the month and +13.6% on the week. GDX/GOLD at the 78th percentile and turning up with acceleration 1.11 says the equity is discounting margin expansion from a $4,000+ gold price that the metal's drawdown has not dented. Energy input costs just fell 13-17% in a week — that is pure miner margin.
trades.trigger: GDX +2.2% today, NEM +13.4% on the week, GDXJ +2.8%, GDX/GOLD +3.0% on a day gold fell 0.8%.
trades.stop: GDX/GOLD closes back below 0.215, or gold breaks 3,800 (then the equity leg goes with it).
